charts.title: GDP contribution of the arts, entertainment and recreation sector in Vietnam from 2015 to 2022
charts.short: GDP contribution of arts, entertainment and recreation in Vietnam 2015-2022
charts.description: In 2022, Vietnam's arts, entertainment and recreation sector accounted for 0.59 percent of the country's total GDP, equivalent to around 56 trillion Vietnamese dong. In that year, Vietnam's total GDP amounted to approximately 9.5 thousand trillion Vietnamese dong.
charts.note: Vietnam; 2015 to 2022; figures at current prices; * Preliminary figures. Read more

charts.title: GDP value of the arts, entertainment and recreation sector in Vietnam from 2015 to 2022 (in trillion Vietnamese dong)
charts.short: GDP value of arts, entertainment and recreation sector in Vietnam 2015-2022
charts.description: In 2022, Vietnam's arts, entertainment, and recreation sector accounted for a GDP value of approximately 56.06 trillion Vietnamese dong, indicating an increase from the previous year. In the same year, Vietnam's GDP amounted to more than 9.5 quadrillion Vietnamese dong.
charts.note: Vietnam; 2015 to 2022; figures at current prices; * Preliminary figures.  Figures have been rounded. The source does not provide data for 2016 and 2017. One thousand Vietnamese dong equals 0.042 U.S. dollars and 0.038 euros as of July [...] Read more

charts.title: Frequency of exercising sports among Vietnamese in 2020
charts.short: Frequency of exercising sports in Vietnam 2020
charts.description: According to a survey on health behaviors, 44 percent of Vietnamese respondents stated that they exercised a lot, very often, moderately, or fairly often. In the same survey, 89 percent of respondents considered themselves very healthy or healthy.
charts.note: Vietnam; October to December 2020; 600 respondents; 18 years and older; covering two provinces

charts.title: Monthly spending on exercises among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Monthly expenditure on exercises among people Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, around 32 percent of the respondents reported to spend less than 300,000 Vietnamese dong per month on exercising. Meanwhile, six percent of them spent over 700,000 Vietnamese dong monthly on exercises.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular exercises among people in Vietnam as of May 2021, by type
charts.short: Most popular exercises in Vietnam 2021, by type
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, fitness was the leading kind of exercise among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 83 percent of them. Meanwhile, 11 percent of them reported doing martial arts as an exercise.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular fitness exercises among people in Vietnam as of May 2021, by type
charts.short: Most popular fitness exercises in Vietnam 2021, by type
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021, walking was the leading kind of fitness exercise among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 66 percent of them. Meanwhile, 28 percent of them reported doing workout as a fitness exercise.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular sports among people in Vietnam as of May 2021, by type
charts.short: Most popular sports in Vietnam 2021, by type
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, football was the leading kind of sport exercise among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 56 percent of them. Meanwhile, 28 percent of them reported doing athletics as a sport exercise.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular martial art exercises among people in Vietnam as of May 2021, by type
charts.short: Most popular martial arts in Vietnam 2021, by type
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, taekwondo and karate were the leading kind of martial arts among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 33 percent of them. Meanwhile, 21 percent of them reported doing Muay Thai.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Main objectives of doing exercise among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Main objectives of exercising among people Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, bones strengthening was the leading objective of doing exercises among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 48 percent of them. Meanwhile, 23 percent of them reported exercising to improve memory.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular fitness locations among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Most popular places to do fitness among people Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, around 46 percent of the respondents reported that they exercised at public locations such as parks. Meanwhile, three percent of them did fitness at specialized schools or classes.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Leading fitness gym brands in Vietnam as of March 2023, by number of studios
charts.short: Leading fitness gym brands Vietnam 2023, by number of studios
charts.description: According to a report by Q&Me, as of March 2023, California Fitness and Yoga was the leading fitness studio chain in Vietnam with 37 studios, followed by Curves with 28 studios, and Elite Fitness with 14 stores. Founded in 2007 by an American entrepreneur, California Fitness and Yoga has become the first and largest international fitness company in Vietnam.
charts.note: Vietnam; as of March 2023

charts.title: Number of fitness chain outlets in Vietnam as of March 2023, by city
charts.short: Number of fitness chain outlets Vietnam 2023, by city
charts.description: According to a report released by Q&Me, as of March 2023, Ho Chi Minh had the highest number of fitness gyms in Vietnam with 55 centers. Meanwhile, there were around 13 gyms in other cities besides Ha Noi and Ho Chi Minh City that year.
charts.note: Vietnam; as of March 2023

charts.title: Frequency of watching sports or fitness videos online among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Frequency of watching sports or fitness videos online among Vietnamese 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, around 45 percent of the respondents stated that they watched online sports and fitness videos often. Meanwhile, around two percent of them never watched these videos.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide

charts.title: Most popular platforms to watch online sport and fitness videos among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Most popular platforms to watch online sport and fitness videos Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, around 78 percent of the respondents stated that they watched online sport and fitness videos using YouTube. Meanwhile, around 18 percent of them watched these video on specialized websites for courses and lessons.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide
categories: Specialized websites for courses and lessons

charts.title: Most popular sport and fitness content online among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Most popular online sport and fitness content Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, around 57 percent of the respondents stated that they watched everyday workout lessons, making these lessons the most popular online sport and fitness content. Meanwhile, around 20 percent of them watched reviews of sport products online.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide
categories: Coaching for a specific part of body

charts.title: Ownership of wearable tech in Vietnam in 2022
charts.short: Ownership of wearable tech in Vietnam 2022
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight, around a third of the respondents stated that they owned a smartwatch while 45 percent of them did not own a smartwatch or wearable fitness or activity tracker. In terms of motivation, the majority of respondents claimed that they were concerned about their health and would like to monitor and improve it by using wearable tech.
charts.note: Vietnam; September 8 to 30, 2022; 3,342 respondents; 16 years and older; among female and male respondents
categories: Yes, both a smartwatch and a fitness/activity tracker

charts.title: Main motivations to purchase wearable tech in Vietnam in 2019
charts.short: Motivations to purchase wearable tech in Vietnam 2019
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight, the majority of respondents claimed that they were concerned about their health and would like to monitor and improve it by using wearable tech. In the same survey, less than half of the respondents stated that they owned a smart wearable.
charts.note: Vietnam; August 2 to 30, 2019; 1,449 respondents; 16 years and older; among female and male respondents that own wearable tech
categories: I am concerned about my health and want to monitor and improve it (such as sleep quality, measuring heart rate, number of steps taken a day, etc)
I am into fitness and want to keep track of and optimize my training and performance
I wanted easier accessibility to smartphone functions without having to constantly have my smartphone in my hand
I already own other smart devices from the same brand (such as smartphones, televisions, etc) and want to stay connected with my other devices easier
The price is reasonable for the functions that it can do
I like to keep up with the latest tech trends and products

charts.title: Frequency of using wearable tech in Vietnam in 2019
charts.short: Frequency of using wearable tech in Vietnam 2019
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight, 65 percent of the respondents claimed that they used their smartwatch or fitness tracker every day. In the same survey, less than half of the respondents stated that they owned a smart wearable.
charts.note: Vietnam; August 2 to 30, 2019; 1,449 respondents; 16 years and older; among female and male respondents that own wearable tech
categories: I rarely use my smartwatch and/or fitness activity tracker
I have stopped using my smartwatch and/or fitness/activity tracker

charts.title: Most common uses for wearable tech in Vietnam in 2019
charts.short: Most common uses for wearable tech in Vietnam 2019
charts.description: According to a survey by Rakuten Insight, 56 percent of respondents claimed that they were monitoring their fitness activities. In the same survey, less than half of the respondents stated that they owned a smart wearable.
charts.note: Vietnam; August 2 to 30, 2019; 1,449 respondents; 16 years and older; among female and male respondents that own wearable tech
categories: Monitor my sleep cycle and set an alarm accordingly
Receive and reply to short text messages
Control and manage other connected devices
Look up and follow directions on a map app

charts.title: Leading non-exercise actions to improve physical conditions among people in Vietnam as of May 2021
charts.short: Most popular actions to improve health Vietnam 2021
charts.description: According to a survey conducted by Q&Me in May 2021 in Vietnam, eating a healthy diet was the leading kind of actions to improve physical conditions among Vietnamese respondents, as stated by 60 percent of them. Meanwhile, 34 percent of them reported quitting smoking and drinking less to improve their health.
charts.note: Vietnam; May 2021; 1,406 respondents; 13-65 years; among respondents nationwide
categories: Drink more water and fewer sugary drinks

charts.title: Volume share of less sweetened liquid milk consumption among consumers in Vietnam from 2018 to 2020
charts.short: Volume share of less sweetened liquid milk consumption Vietnam 2018-2020
charts.description: As of the third quarter of 2020, less sweetened liquid milk accounted for 12.5 percent of milk consumption volume among Vietnamese consumers. The share of less sweetened liquid milk volume had been growing steadily within the observed timeline.
charts.note: Vietnam; MAT Q3 2018 to MAT Q3 2020; among respondents in Ho Chi Minh City, Ha Noi, Da Nang and Can Tho

charts.title: Volume share of plain liquid milk consumption among consumers in Vietnam from 2018 to 2020
charts.short: Volume share of plain liquid milk consumption Vietnam 2018-2020
charts.description: As of the third quarter of 2020, plain liquid milk accounted for 20.4 percent of milk consumption volume among Vietnamese consumers. The share of plain liquid milk volume had been growing steadily within the observed timeline as more consumers had been choosing no-sugar-added products.
charts.note: Vietnam; MAT Q3 2018 to MAT Q3 2020; among respondents in Ho Chi Minh City, Ha Noi, Da Nang and Can Tho

charts.title: Value share of plant based nutrition drinks in Vietnam as of 3rd quarter 2020, by type
charts.short: Value share of plant based drinks Vietnam Q3 2020, by type
charts.description: As of the third quarter of 2020, soya-based products accounted for the majority of the value share of plant-based nutrition drinks in Vietnam, with a share of 83 percent. Meanwhile, rice-based products had a value share of six percent in the same period.
charts.note: Vietnam; MAT Q3 2020; among respondents in Ho Chi Minh City, Ha Noi, Da Nang and Can Tho
